newsitem.title: JAPAN: EMU may benefit Asian currencies - SIMEX official.
newsitem.headline: EMU may benefit Asian currencies - SIMEX official.

text.p: European economic and monetary union (EMU) and the new European currency may benefit Asian currencies, said Elizabeth Sam, deputy chairman of the Singapore International Monetary Exchange Limited (SIMEX).

Speaking at a symposium in Tokyo on Monday, Sam said: "The diminishing opportunities in European currencies and bond markets (as a result of EMU) will lead to increased interest in Asian regional currencies."
"This will be enhanced by the growth of these economies and increasing liberalisation which will result in more liquid markets for these currencies," she added.

EMU and the introduction of the Euro, the single European currency, are set for January 1, 1999. Expectations are that EMU will initially include Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.

Although some Tokyo financial analysts feel the role of the yen may be reduced after the advent of the Euro, Sam said she thought the yen could become a more important reserve currency than it is now due to market concerns about the new currency.
But David Hale, economist at Zurich Kemper Investments and another speaker at the symposium, disagreed. "I think the Euro will be number two in the world reserve market."
He added that if Asian countries do decide to shift their emphasis away from the dollar, they won't necessarily shift to the yen but are likely to favour a mixed basket of currencies.

Tomomitsu Oba, a former vice minister of international affairs at Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF), cautioned that at this point it is hard to see how strong the Euro will be and how its value will be set.
"Until we actually get to the year 2000 and see what takes place, it is difficult to say anything clearly," he said.
